cafc-wallet.title: Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre bulletin: Cryptocurrency wallet fraud (via FCNB)
cafc-wallet.supports: Never share a recovery phrase; legitimate support never asks for it; unsolicited contact, 'verify/connect your wallet' links, remote-access requests and 'move to this wallet' are warning signs.

ftc-crypto.title: FTC: What To Know About Cryptocurrency and Scams
ftc-crypto.supports: Scammers impersonate companies; don't click links in unexpected messages; only scammers demand crypto; free-crypto giveaways are fake.

ftc-phishing.title: FTC: How To Recognize and Avoid Phishing Scams
ftc-phishing.supports: Urgency and links are signs; contact companies through a site or app you know is real; real companies won't send a link asking you to update details.

ftc-impersonator.title: FTC: What To Know About Cryptocurrency and Scams
ftc-impersonator.supports: Legitimate businesses never message you on social media demanding money or crypto.

ftc-tech-support.title: Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre bulletin: Cryptocurrency wallet fraud (via FCNB)
ftc-tech-support.supports: Requests to install software or give remote access are warning signs.

ftc-family.title: FTC: Family emergency scams (advice and alerts)
ftc-family.supports: Check with the family member on a number you already know before sending money.

ftc-jobs.title: FTC: Task scams create the illusion of making money
ftc-jobs.supports: Real jobs never make you pay to start earning.

europol-report.title: Europol: Report cybercrime online (links to each EU country's reporting site)
europol-report.supports: Europe: report online fraud through your country's official police reporting site, listed by Europol; where there is no online option, go to the local police.

ic3-2024.title: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center: 2024 Internet Crime Report (summary)
ic3-2024.supports: Investment fraud was the largest loss category ($6.57B); crypto investment fraud $5.8B; crypto-related losses $9.32B.

ftc-data-2024.title: FTC: New data show a big jump in reported losses to fraud (2024)
ftc-data-2024.supports: Investment scams: highest losses ($5.7B). Imposter scams: most reported. Job scam losses and reports rising sharply.

chainalysis-2025.title: Chainalysis 2025 Crypto Crime Report: scams (summary)
chainalysis-2025.supports: Relationship-investment ('pig butchering') scams led crypto scam revenue in 2024, up 40%.

ftc-shipping.title: FTC: Fake shipping notification emails and text messages
ftc-shipping.supports: Delivery-problem messages with a link are a common scam; don't click; check the retailer's own site or contact the shipper using a phone number or website you know is real.

ftc-tolls.title: FTC: Got a text about unpaid tolls? It's probably a scam
ftc-tolls.supports: Unexpected texts demanding toll payment are scams; don't click or respond; check with the tolling agency using contact details you already know; report junk texts and delete.

ftc-bank-call.title: FTC: Got a call about fraud activity on your bank account? It could be a scammer
ftc-bank-call.supports: Never move money to 'protect' it; never share a verification code; check by calling your real bank on a number from your statement; bank accounts have fewer protections than credit cards.

ftc-codes.title: FTC: What's a verification code and why would someone ask me for it?
ftc-codes.supports: Anyone who asks for your verification code is a scammer; the code is only for you to log in; end the contact and contact your bank yourself.

ftc-government.title: FTC: How to avoid a government impersonation scam
ftc-government.supports: Government agencies never call, email, text or message to ask for money or personal information; caller ID can be faked; verify by calling the agency on a number you know is correct; gift cards, crypto and wire transfers are scam payment methods.

ftc-techsupport.title: FTC: How to spot, avoid, and report tech support scams
ftc-techsupport.supports: Real pop-ups never ask you to call a number; search ads can show scam numbers; no real support needs remote access plus payment by gift card or transfer; contact the company on a number you know is real.

ftc-customerservice.title: FTC: Scammers and 'customer service': another imposter scam
ftc-customerservice.supports: Scammers pay to put fake customer-service numbers in search results; use the number in your manual or on the box or type the official website yourself; no real company asks for gift cards or wire transfers.

ftc-spamtexts.title: FTC: How to recognize and report spam text messages
ftc-spamtexts.supports: Legitimate companies won't ask for account information by text; don't click links; use a number or website you know is real; report spam texts to your provider and to the fraud-reporting site.

ftc-utility.title: FTC: Scammers pretend to be your utility company
ftc-utility.supports: Scammers threaten shutoff to rush you; real utilities don't demand same-day payment; they ask for wire, crypto, payment apps or gift cards; contact the company using the number on your bill or its website; paid search ads can lead to impersonators.

in-pib-alert.title: Press Information Bureau (India): Alert against incidents of blackmail and digital arrest
in-pib-alert.supports: Criminals pose as police and other agencies, claim a parcel with illegal goods was sent in your name or a relative is in custody, demand money, and keep victims on video calls; report at once on helpline 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.

in-1930.title: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (India): helpline 1930
in-1930.supports: Toll-free helpline 1930 and the portal cybercrime.gov.in are where to report cyber fraud in India.

in-rbi-beaware.title: Reserve Bank of India Ombudsman booklet: BE(A)WARE
in-rbi-beaware.supports: Never share OTP, PIN, CVV or passwords; KYC-update calls and links are a common trick, so use the official website or branch; never pay a processing fee in advance for a loan or prize; install a screen-sharing app only on advice of the official number on the company website; report fraud quickly on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.

in-certin-booklet.title: CERT-In: Cyber Security Awareness Booklet for Digital Nagriks
in-certin-booklet.supports: Download apps only from trusted sources or the official app store; do not install apps through links on chats or social media; never share an OTP, PIN or CVV, nor an OTP or UPI PIN to receive money; do not install remote access apps on the pretext of help.

in-sebi-dos.title: SEBI Investor: Securities market do and dont
in-sebi-dos.supports: Deal only with registered intermediaries; take investment advice from a registered adviser; do not base decisions on hot tips; beware Ponzi and unregistered deposit schemes.

ftc-job-scams.title: FTC: Job Scams
ftc-job-scams.supports: Honest employers never ask you to pay to get a job; big pay for little work is a warning; reshipping and forwarding jobs are scams; a check with a request to send part back is a scam; search the company name with scam or review.

ftc-romance.title: FTC: Romance Scams
ftc-romance.supports: Unsolicited contact, pressure to move off the platform, living far away for work or service, and money requests are red flags; never send money, gift cards, wire transfers or crypto to an online love interest.

ftc-gift-cards.title: FTC: Avoiding and Reporting Gift Card Scams
ftc-gift-cards.supports: No honest business or agency makes you buy a gift card to pay; never send money to someone you have not met; check with a friend or relative on a number you know.

ftc-prize.title: FTC: Fake Prize, Sweepstakes and Lottery Scams
ftc-prize.supports: Real prizes are free; fees for taxes or shipping to collect a prize are a scam; winning a contest you never entered is a warning; pressure to act fast; delete and report.

ftc-rental.title: FTC: Rental Listing Scams
ftc-rental.supports: A price far below nearby rents, a deposit before you see the place, pressure, and wire, gift card or crypto payment are red flags; search the address and owner name.

ftc-marketplace.title: FTC: Buying From an Online Marketplace
ftc-marketplace.supports: Use a safer payment method with buyer protection; avoid wire, gift card and crypto payment; do not pay outside the marketplace payment system.

ftc-invest-social.title: FTC: Can you spot an investment scam on social media?
ftc-invest-social.supports: Promises of big returns and pressure to act fast, thin details and a request to pay by crypto or a payment app are red flags; there are no guaranteed returns; research the offer and contact your friend another way.
